title: Build discovery case: the contract for one fixture folder
$comment: docs/plans/build-discovery-test-program-2026-11-08.md section 2 and 3. A case is a folder (tree/) and this expectation. Every path in the tree has exactly one role; units and non-units are named with evidence and reasons; pending names the checks the runtime does not meet yet by registry sub-item and the runner treats them as strict xfails.

matrix.description: The matrix cell this case exercises (plan section 4).

mirrors.description: The real-world target or shape this case mirrors.

condition.description: The condition the point is defined under, as discovery records it (selects among same-named points).

language.description: The language the point compiles, when asserted.

sources.description: Exact source list of the point, when asserted.

build_points_exact.description: When true, build_points is the complete (name, kind) list: a unit with none has an empty list and this flag.

facts.description: Subset of the unit's facts that must be present with these values (workspace, descriptor_facts, language, ...).

facts_absent.description: Fact keys that must be absent or empty on the unit (a negative twin asserts the relation is not stated).

build_system.description: When given, no unit with this root and system may exist; otherwise no unit at this root at all.

marker.description: The look-alike file; its assignment is asserted through assignment or role.

role.description: The role the look-alike must have instead.

assignment.description: path -> role for paths asserted individually.

assignment_defaults.description: glob -> role for paths not listed individually; first match wins. Together with assignment they must cover every path in the tree.

orphaned_sources.description: Exact orphan list when asserted: path, language, reason, nearest unit root (or null).

exclusions.description: policy name -> globs excluded before discovery; excluded paths take the role excluded:<policy>.

pending.description: Checks the runtime does not meet yet. check is a check id the runner prints; ref is a registry id or sub-item.
